Use a mixed instances policy with many instance types and Availability Zones and the price-capacity-optimized strategy
Keep the single instance type and choose the lowest-price allocation strategy for the Spot capacity
Request Spot Instances with a defined duration of six hours so that they are not interrupted
questions.explanation: Option B is correct because diversifying across many instance types and Availability Zones gives access to many Spot capacity pools, and the price-capacity-optimized strategy selects pools that have both low prices and low chance of interruption. Option A is incorrect because Reserved Instances would forgo the Spot savings and commit the company for the whole fleet. Option C is incorrect because a single instance type in the lowest-price pool is more likely to be interrupted. Option D is incorrect because Spot Instances with a defined duration (Spot blocks) are no longer available. Takeaway: diversify Spot capacity pools to reduce interruptions.

questions.question: A company runs a three-tier application in us-east-1. The disaster recovery objective is to serve production traffic from us-west-2 within a few minutes after a Regional failure, with data loss under one minute. The standby environment must also accept a small percentage of live traffic continuously so that the team knows it works. The company does not want to pay for a full-size active-active deployment. Which DR strategy should the solutions architect choose?
options: Multi-site active-active, with the full production stack running and scaled for all traffic in both Regions
Pilot light, with only the replicated database running in us-west-2 and application servers launched after a failure
Backup and restore, with the stack re-created from cross-Region backups and infrastructure templates after a failure
Warm standby, with a scaled-down but fully functional copy of the stack running in us-west-2 and replicated data
questions.explanation: Option D is correct because warm standby keeps a fully functional, scaled-down environment running, so it can receive a small share of traffic at all times and scale up quickly during failover. Option A is incorrect because it meets the objectives but at the cost of a full-size second deployment, which the company wants to avoid. Option B is incorrect because in pilot light only core components such as the database are running, so the application tier cannot serve traffic until it is provisioned. Option C is incorrect because backup and restore has the longest recovery time and no running environment. Takeaway: DR cost and recovery speed increase from backup and restore to pilot light to warm standby to active-active.

questions.question: Several producer services publish business events to a single Amazon SNS topic. Three consumer teams each own an Amazon SQS queue subscribed to the topic, and each team needs only events whose eventType message attribute matches its domain. The producers must not change, and the consumers should not need code to discard irrelevant events. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: Have every consumer read all messages from its queue and delete the events that it does not need
Add a subscription filter policy on eventType to each queue's SNS subscription
Create a separate SNS topic for each event type and require the producers to publish to the matching topic
Subscribe an AWS Lambda function to the topic that filters each event and forwards it to the correct queue
questions.explanation: Option B is correct because SNS subscription filter policies evaluate message attributes and deliver only matching messages to each subscriber, with no changes to producers or consumer code. Option A is incorrect because consumers still receive, and pay to process, every event, and the requirement says consumers should not need code to discard events. Option C is incorrect because it requires every producer to change how it publishes. Option D is incorrect because it adds a component to build, scale, and monitor for something SNS does natively. Takeaway: use SNS message filtering to route different subsets of a topic to different subscribers.

questions.question: An Amazon Aurora MySQL cluster in us-east-1 supports a business-critical application. A regulator requires a disaster recovery capability in eu-west-1 with an RPO measured in seconds and a fast, low-effort promotion of the European Region during an outage. The team does not want to run custom replication tooling. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: Configure binary log replication from the cluster to a new Aurora cluster in eu-west-1 and promote the new cluster during an outage
Use AWS Backup to copy Aurora cluster backups to eu-west-1 every hour and restore the newest backup during an outage
Create an Aurora global database with a secondary cluster in eu-west-1 and promote the secondary cluster during a Regional outage
Add Aurora Replicas in additional Availability Zones of us-east-1 and promote a replica during an outage
questions.explanation: Option C is correct because Aurora global database replicates at the storage layer to secondary Regions with typical lag of under a second (RPO measured in seconds), and a secondary cluster can be promoted with low effort. Option A is incorrect because binary log replication is logical replication that you manage, and it typically has more lag and operational overhead. Option B is incorrect because hourly backup copies give an RPO of up to an hour and a slower restore. Option D is incorrect because replicas in the same Region do not protect against a Regional outage. Takeaway: Aurora global database is the built-in cross-Region DR and low-latency read option for Aurora.

questions.question: A company must copy an encrypted Amazon EBS snapshot to a disaster recovery account. The snapshot is encrypted by using a customer managed KMS key in the source account. The DR account must be able to restore volumes from the snapshot and must not depend on the source account's key afterwards. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: Share the snapshot and grant the DR account use of the KMS key, then have the DR account copy the snapshot and re-encrypt it with its own key
Share a snapshot that is encrypted with the AWS managed key aws/ebs with the DR account and let the DR account restore volumes directly
Make the encrypted snapshot public so that the DR account can copy it without additional key permissions or account-level sharing
Export the snapshot data to an unencrypted S3 bucket in the DR account and re-create the volumes from the exported objects
questions.explanation: Option A is correct because an encrypted snapshot can be shared only when it uses a customer managed key, the target account must be allowed to use that key, and the target account can then create its own copy encrypted with its own key, removing the dependency on the source key. Option B is incorrect because snapshots encrypted with an AWS managed key cannot be shared with other accounts. Option C is incorrect because encrypted snapshots cannot be made public. Option D is incorrect because EBS snapshots cannot be exported this way, and storing the data unencrypted violates the encryption requirement. Takeaway: use a customer managed key for snapshots that must be shared across accounts.

questions.question: A company shares an 80 TB public research dataset in an Amazon S3 bucket with 200 partner organizations that have their own AWS accounts. The company wants the partners to pay for the requests and data transfer they generate, and partners can access the bucket with their own IAM identities. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: Enable Requester Pays on the bucket and have partners send authenticated requests that acknowledge the charges
Enable Requester Pays on the bucket and allow anonymous public access so that partners do not need credentials
Put an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the bucket so that CloudFront bills the partners
Apply cost allocation tags to the bucket and invoice the partners based on the tagged usage
questions.explanation: Option A is correct because with Requester Pays enabled the requester, rather than the bucket owner, pays for the request and data transfer costs, and requesters must be authenticated and include the request-payer acknowledgment in their requests. Option B is incorrect because anonymous requests are not allowed on Requester Pays buckets, since AWS must identify the account to charge. Option C is incorrect because CloudFront charges the distribution owner, not the viewers. Option D is incorrect because cost allocation tags only report the bucket owner's costs and do not shift charges to other accounts. Takeaway: Requester Pays moves data transfer and request costs to authenticated requesters.

questions.question: A mobile application lets users sign in with a social identity provider and then upload profile photos directly to Amazon S3. Each user must be able to access only the objects under their own prefix, and the app must not contain long-term AWS credentials. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: Create an IAM user for each app user with a policy for the user's prefix and store the access keys in the device's secure storage
Create one IAM role for all authenticated users with S3 read and write access, and let the app code enforce the prefix restriction
Use an Amazon Cognito identity pool that maps authenticated users to an IAM role whose policy limits S3 access to the prefix matching the user's identity ID
Use an Amazon Cognito user pool only, and send the ID token from the app as the credential for S3 requests from the mobile client
questions.explanation: Option C is correct because an identity pool exchanges tokens from a supported provider, or from a user pool, for temporary AWS credentials, and the role policy can use the Cognito identity ID policy variable to scope each user to a prefix. Option A is incorrect because it places long-term credentials on devices and does not scale. Option B is incorrect because a shared role with client-side enforcement lets a modified app read every user's data. Option D is incorrect because a user pool issues JSON web tokens for authenticating to your own application and services such as API Gateway; S3 does not accept those tokens as credentials. Takeaway: user pools authenticate users; identity pools authorize them to AWS resources with temporary credentials.

questions.question: A company must encrypt in transit all traffic between its data center and AWS. It has a 10 Gbps dedicated Direct Connect connection and a separate 1 Gbps hosted Direct Connect connection. The encryption solution for the dedicated connection must deliver near line-rate throughput. Which TWO actions meet these requirements? (Select TWO)
options: Establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN over the 1 Gbps hosted connection to provide IPsec encryption
Rely on the private virtual interface, because Direct Connect encrypts traffic by default
Enable MAC Security (MACsec) on the 10 Gbps dedicated connection
Enable MACsec on the 1 Gbps hosted connection
Enable EBS encryption on the instances that communicate with the data center
questions.explanation: Options A and C are correct. MACsec provides layer 2 encryption at near line rate and is supported on dedicated connections at supported speeds such as 10 Gbps, while an IPsec Site-to-Site VPN can run over a Direct Connect connection to encrypt traffic on connections where MACsec is not available. Option B is incorrect because Direct Connect provides a private path but does not encrypt traffic by default. Option D is incorrect because MACsec is available only for dedicated connections, not for hosted connections. Option E is incorrect because EBS encryption protects data at rest and does not encrypt data in transit across the network link. Takeaway: MACsec for dedicated high-speed ports, IPsec VPN over Direct Connect for other cases.

questions.question: A security team must deploy third-party virtual firewall appliances that inspect all traffic entering and leaving several VPCs. The appliances use the GENEVE protocol, must be inserted transparently into the traffic path, and must scale horizontally with health checking. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: Deploy a Gateway Load Balancer with the appliances as targets and route traffic through Gateway Load Balancer endpoints
Place the appliances behind a Network Load Balancer and update the route tables to send traffic to the NLB
Place the appliances behind an Application Load Balancer and use path-based routing to steer the traffic
Route all traffic to the elastic network interface of a single appliance instance and update the route on failure
questions.explanation: Option A is correct because Gateway Load Balancer combines a transparent network gateway and a load balancer: it sends traffic to virtual appliances using GENEVE, health-checks the targets, and scales them horizontally, with endpoints in the traffic path. Option B is incorrect because a Network Load Balancer is not a bump-in-the-wire that preserves the original packets and does not use GENEVE encapsulation. Option C is incorrect because an Application Load Balancer terminates HTTP and HTTPS connections at layer 7 and is not transparent to other traffic. Option D is incorrect because a single appliance is a single point of failure and does not scale. Takeaway: use Gateway Load Balancer for inline third-party security appliances.

questions.question: A company uses AWS Organizations with 40 member accounts. The security team requires that no principal in any member account, including account administrators, can stop AWS CloudTrail logging or delete the GuardDuty detector. Only a dedicated security-automation role may perform these actions. Which solution enforces this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: Attach an IAM permissions boundary that denies cloudtrail:StopLogging, cloudtrail:DeleteTrail, and guardduty:DeleteDetector to every IAM role in each member account, except the security-automation role
Create an IAM policy that denies cloudtrail:StopLogging, cloudtrail:DeleteTrail, and guardduty:DeleteDetector in each member account and attach it to every administrator group and role
Attach an SCP to the organization root that denies cloudtrail:StopLogging, cloudtrail:DeleteTrail, and guardduty:DeleteDetector for every principal except the security-automation role
Deploy AWS Config rules in each member account that detect a stopped trail or a deleted detector and run automatic remediation to restart logging and recreate the detector
questions.explanation: Option C is correct because an SCP is a preventive guardrail that applies to every IAM user and role in the member accounts, including administrators, and it is managed once from the organization. A condition on the caller (for example aws:PrincipalArn) exempts the security-automation role. Option A is incorrect because a permissions boundary must be attached to each role individually, is not applied to new roles automatically, and can be changed by anyone with the right IAM permissions inside the account. Option B is incorrect because identity policies are managed per account, cover only the groups they are attached to, and can be detached by account administrators. Option D is incorrect because AWS Config is detective: the trail is already stopped before remediation runs, so logging gaps occur. Takeaway: SCPs set the maximum permissions for member accounts and are the tool for organization-wide preventive controls (they do not affect the management account).

questions.question: A compliance rule states that every request to an Amazon S3 bucket must use TLS, and every stored object must be encrypted at rest with the company's customer managed AWS KMS key. Which TWO actions meet these requirements? (Select TWO)
options: Enable Amazon Macie on the bucket so that unencrypted objects are encrypted automatically
Add a bucket policy statement that denies all requests when the aws:SecureTransport condition key is false
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the bucket so that all requests use HTTPS
Configure default encryption on the bucket to use SSE-KMS with the customer managed key
Enable S3 Block Public Access on the bucket to require encrypted connections
questions.explanation: Options B and D are correct. Denying requests where aws:SecureTransport is false rejects plain HTTP requests, and default encryption with SSE-KMS applies the customer managed key to new objects that do not specify encryption. Option A is incorrect because Macie discovers and reports sensitive data and does not encrypt objects. Option C is incorrect because Transfer Acceleration speeds up transfers and does not enforce TLS. Option E is incorrect because Block Public Access prevents public access through ACLs and policies but has no effect on the transport protocol or the encryption of objects. Takeaway: enforce TLS with a bucket policy condition and enforce encryption at rest with default bucket encryption.

questions.question: A company with an AWS Organization wants to allocate monthly costs to 12 product teams. Resources carry a team tag, but the team tag does not appear as a grouping option in AWS Cost Explorer. The company also wants tag keys and values to be consistent across accounts. Which TWO actions meet these requirements? (Select TWO)
options: Enable AWS Config in each account so that costs are attributed to tags automatically
Activate the team tag as a user-defined cost allocation tag in the management account's billing settings
Create an AWS Organizations tag policy that defines the allowed tag key and values
Enable AWS Trusted Advisor cost optimization checks to group charges by the team tag
Create an AWS Budgets action that adds the team tag to resources that lack it
questions.explanation: Options B and C are correct. A user-defined tag appears in cost reports and Cost Explorer only after it is activated as a cost allocation tag in the Billing and Cost Management console, and tag policies standardize tag keys and allowed values across the accounts in an organization. Option A is incorrect because AWS Config records resource configuration and does not attribute costs. Option D is incorrect because Trusted Advisor provides recommendations and does not group charges by tag. Option E is incorrect because a Budgets action responds to cost thresholds and does not tag resources by team. Takeaway: tag, activate the tag for cost allocation, and standardize the tags with policies.

questions.question: Hundreds of containers and functions read and write a shared file system through NFS. Activity is idle for hours and then bursts to several GiB/s. The file system holds only about 200 GiB of data, and the team cannot predict burst sizes. Which Amazon EFS configuration meets the performance requirement with the LEAST management effort?
options: Max I/O performance mode with Elastic throughput
General Purpose performance mode with Bursting throughput
General Purpose performance mode with Provisioned throughput sized to the expected peak
General Purpose performance mode with Elastic throughput
questions.explanation: Option D is correct because Elastic throughput scales automatically with the workload up to the Regional limits, requires no capacity planning, and is intended for spiky or unpredictable workloads. Option A is incorrect because Max I/O mode is not supported with Elastic throughput, and it has higher latency than General Purpose mode. Option B is incorrect because Bursting throughput scales with the amount of data stored; a 200 GiB file system has a baseline of about 10 MiB/s and a limited burst credit balance. Option C is incorrect because Provisioned throughput requires you to estimate and pay for the throughput continuously, which does not suit unpredictable bursts. Takeaway: default to General Purpose with Elastic throughput for spiky, unpredictable EFS workloads.
